sentences.zh: 他所有的赌注都得到了回报。

sentences.en: There is talk that he is called your highness by his fellows.
sentences.zh: 有传言说他被同僚称为“殿下”。

sentences.en: There's talk that he's going to award his captain's knighthoods.
sentences.zh: 有传言说他要授予他的船长们骑士爵位。

sentences.en: There are even some rumors that he will call himself a king.
sentences.zh: 甚至有传言说他会自称为王。

sentences.en: He's so far away from Spain.
sentences.zh: 他离西班牙太远了。

sentences.en: Of course, he doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 当然，他没那么做。

sentences.en: He's always a bit anxious because, of course, he has broken the law.
sentences.zh: 他总是有点焦虑，因为他毕竟触犯了法律。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he has the fat and jolly Velázquez.
sentences.zh: 而且他还有那个肥胖又快活的贝拉斯克斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Back in Cuba to deal with.
sentences.zh: 还得回古巴去应付他。

sentences.en: I know, Tom, what you're thinking.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在想什么，汤姆。

sentences.en: You're thinking that you're Cortes and I'm Velázquez.
sentences.zh: 你在想你是科尔特斯，而我是贝拉斯克斯。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not saying it, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可没这么说，没有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You're cruel, rapacious, and ultimately a cold person.
sentences.zh: 你残忍、贪婪，骨子里是个冷酷的人。

sentences.en: I'm a great hospitable guy.
sentences.zh: 我可是个热情好客的人。

sentences.en: No, I was thinking more that I'm Moctezuma and you're Cortes.
sentences.zh: 不，我其实是在想，我是蒙特祖马，而你是科尔特斯。

sentences.en: You're a formidable...
sentences.zh: 你真是个可怕的……

sentences.en: You've taken me prisoner and forcing me to do endless episodes on the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 你把我俘虏了，还逼着我没完没了地录制关于阿兹特克人的节目。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That's so harsh because I'm desperate to do them as well.
sentences.zh: 这太刻薄了，因为我也非常想做这些节目。

sentences.en: It's an unworthy joke.
sentences.zh: 这玩笑开得真不地道。

sentences.en: So when I'm gone, you'll say of me, ultimately a mediocre and dishonest man.
sentences.zh: 所以等我走了，你一定会说我是一个平庸且不诚实的人。

sentences.en: A bad man.
sentences.zh: 一个坏人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And a mediocre.
sentences.zh: 而且是个平庸之辈。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, this particular mediocre man, although I don't think he is mediocre, I think he is a terrifyingly ruthless opportuniSt. So that autumn, to Velázquez's horror,
sentences.zh: 好吧，总之，这个所谓的平庸之辈——虽然我不觉得他平庸，我觉得他是一个极其冷酷无情的机会主义者。所以那年秋天，在贝拉斯克斯的惊恐中，

sentences.en: Charles V confirms Cortes as governor, captain general.
sentences.zh: 查理五世确认了科尔特斯作为总督和总队长的身份。

sentences.en: Because the scale of his achievement is evident, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是因为他取得的成就显而易见吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think he has no choice.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他别无选择。

sentences.en: Rather than the wealth that he's sending.
sentences.zh: 而不是因为他送回来的那些财富。

sentences.en: I mean, he is sending some wealth.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他确实送回了一些财富。

sentences.en: He's sending something.
sentences.zh: 他送回了东西。

sentences.en: He's not sending nothing.
sentences.zh: 他不是什么都没送。

sentences.en: But I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你是对的。

sentences.en: The stories that are going back to Europe, I mean, it must seem barely believable.
sentences.zh: 传回欧洲的那些故事，我是说，一定让人难以置信。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Is Cortes a hero across Europe?
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯在欧洲被视为英雄吗？

sentences.en: This is the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 这正是最有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Even at this point, it's not modern wokery to say Cortes is a very, very ambiguous, if not downright dislikable figure.
sentences.zh: 即便在当时，说科尔特斯是一个非常、非常复杂，甚至令人反感的人物，也不是什么现代的“觉醒文化”。

sentences.en: Because even at the time, I think there is an unease.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在那个时代，我认为也存在一种不安。

sentences.en: You know, I think Charles V, for example, would say that he is very uneasy with the idea of kind of rampaging in to somebody else's kingdom, toppling them, and just taking it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得查理五世，比如他，会对那种闯入别人的王国、推翻统治并直接据为己有的想法感到非常不安。

sentences.en: Kings don't tend to like that kind of behaviour.
sentences.zh: 国王们通常不喜欢那种行为。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because all the legalism that surrounds the narrative of Moctezuma handing over his empire to the king, I mean, who cares what the Mexica think among the Spaniards?
sentences.zh: 因为围绕着蒙特祖马将帝国移交给国王的叙事，所有的法律条文——我是说，在西班牙人中间，谁在乎墨西加人怎么想？

sentences.en: It's about how they're presenting it to people back in Europe.
sentences.zh: 关键在于他们如何向欧洲的人们展示这一切。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It needs to seem legal.
sentences.zh: 它必须看起来合法。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It cannot just be a ruthless land grab.
sentences.zh: 它不能仅仅是一场无情的土地掠夺。

sentences.en: So even at this point, in the early decades of European colonialism, there is a sense that just to barge in willy-nilly, kill everybody and take their lands is wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在那个时候，在欧洲殖民主义的早期几十年里，人们也有一种感觉：仅仅是横冲直撞、杀光所有人并夺取土地是错误的。

sentences.en: You have to have a legal pretext.
sentences.zh: 你必须有一个合法的借口。

sentences.en: And that's why there's all this fiction of Moctezuma surrendering his kingdom and then the Aztecs being incited into this disgraceful rebellion.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么会有关于蒙特祖马投降王国，然后阿兹特克人被煽动进行可耻叛乱的种种虚构故事。

sentences.en: And also, this is laying foundations for the sense that indigenous peoples do have rights to the lands that they inhabit.
sentences.zh: 而且，这也为原住民对其居住的土地拥有权利这一观念奠定了基础。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which will be woven into the international law that emerges in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这后来被编织进了19世纪出现的国际法中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And by the way, jumping ahead of ourselves, people like the Tlaxcalans, they are very jealous of those legal rights and their role as allies of the Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们超前一点说，像特拉斯卡拉人这样的人，他们非常珍视那些法律权利，以及他们作为西班牙人盟友的角色。

sentences.en: And they maintain it for many, many years to come, centuries to come, that they are self-governing.
sentences.zh: 而且在未来的许多年、许多世纪里，他们都坚持自己是自治的。

sentences.en: They have special privileges under the Spanish crown and they do.
sentences.zh: 他们在西班牙王室治下享有特权，事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: And if they're ever challenged, they go to law, they go to court.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的权利受到挑战，他们就会诉诸法律，诉诸法庭。

sentences.en: They will send people to Spain to fight for their rights.
sentences.zh: 他们会派人去西班牙为自己的权利而战。

sentences.en: And the Spanish will often acknowledge that.
sentences.zh: 而西班牙人通常也会承认这一点。

sentences.en: So the legalism is not just a fantasy or a fiction.
sentences.zh: 所以这种法律主义不仅仅是幻想或虚构。

sentences.en: It's real.
sentences.zh: 它是真实的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And that is the kind of the paradox of it, that the crimes of the conquistadors are judged by the same legal system that the Spanish are also bringing in.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中的悖论，征服者的罪行是由西班牙人带来的同一套法律体系来审判的。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And that's another theme throughout European colonialism.
sentences.zh: 这也是贯穿欧洲殖民主义的另一个主题。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: On Cortez himself.
sentences.zh: 回到科尔特斯本人身上。

sentences.en: Some of our very keenest listeners may remember
sentences.zh: 我们一些非常敏锐的听众可能还记得，

sentences.en: Cortez actually has a wife.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯其实是有妻子的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我知道。

sentences.en: Since episode one, Cortez has a wife that Velazquez had forced him to marry on Cuba,
sentences.zh: 从第一集开始，科尔特斯就有一个贝拉斯克斯强迫他在古巴娶的妻子，

sentences.en: Catalina Suarez.
sentences.zh: 卡塔琳娜·苏亚雷斯。

sentences.en: Now she has been waiting all this time to find out what's going on with her husband, who's off in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 现在她已经等了这么久，想知道在墨西哥的丈夫到底怎么样了。

sentences.en: She hears the news that he's won and he doesn't call for her.
sentences.zh: 她听到他获胜的消息，但他却没有召她过去。

sentences.en: And eventually she runs out of patience and she and her sister travel to Tenochtitlán themselves.
sentences.zh: 最终她失去了耐心，和她的姐妹亲自前往特诺奇蒂特兰。

sentences.en: And they get there late summer, early autumn.
sentences.zh: 她们在夏末秋初到达了那里。

sentences.en: Oh, hello, darling.
sentences.zh: 哦，你好啊，亲爱的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now she is welcomed as a queen.
sentences.zh: 现在她被当作王后一样欢迎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, people say, gosh, Cortez's wife, the wife of his highness Cortez, the new master.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们会说，天哪，科尔特斯的妻子，科尔特斯大人的妻子，新的主人。

sentences.en: Hurrah, hurrah for her.
sentences.zh: 万岁，为她欢呼。

sentences.en: His mansion, the accounts that we have, there are rumours and stories that his mansion in Coyoacán is already filled with various women.
sentences.zh: 他的宅邸，根据我们现有的记录，有传言和故事说他在科约阿坎的宅邸里已经住满了各种女人。

sentences.en: And what about Malinche?
sentences.zh: 那马林切呢？

sentences.en: Malinche, almost certainly among them.
sentences.zh: 马林切几乎肯定就在其中。

sentences.en: Malinche is pregnant at this point.
sentences.zh: 马林切此时已经怀孕了。

sentences.en: And not long after Catalina's arrival, Malinche gives birth to a little boy whom she christens Martin Cortez.
sentences.zh: 在卡塔琳娜到达后不久，马林切生下了一个小男孩，她给他起名叫马丁·科尔特斯。

sentences.en: So that's kind of giving the game away a bit.
sentences.zh: 这算是把底牌给露出来了。

sentences.en: And then something extraordinary happens.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件非同寻常的事。

sentences.en: On All Saints Day, the 1st of November,
sentences.zh: 在万圣节，也就是11月1日，

sentences.en: Cortez holds a party at his house in Coyoacán.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯在他科约阿坎的家中举办了一场派对。

sentences.en: There's music and stuff, dancing and all this.
sentences.zh: 有音乐之类的，还有跳舞等等。

sentences.en: And Cortez and Catalina are seen quarrelling or exchanging harsh words or something.
sentences.zh: 有人看到科尔特斯和卡塔琳娜在争吵，或者说了些刻薄的话之类的。

sentences.en: And she goes to bed before him and then he follows.
sentences.zh: 然后她比他先上床休息，随后他也跟了过去。

sentences.en: And in the middle of the night, he wakes the house and he says, a terrible thing has happened.
sentences.zh: 半夜里，他叫醒了全家，说，发生了一件可怕的事。

sentences.en: I found my wife dead in her room.
sentences.zh: 我发现我妻子死在房间里了。

sentences.en: She must have had a fit.
sentences.zh: 她一定是发病了。

sentences.en: I knew she had a very weak heart.
sentences.zh: 我知道她心脏很弱。

sentences.en: What a terrible business.
sentences.zh: 真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: She must have accidentally thrown herself out of the window kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 她一定是意外从窗户掉下去了之类的。

sentences.en: Exactly that.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Very few people are allowed to see her body.
sentences.zh: 很少有人被允许看到她的遗体。

sentences.en: She's buried in great haste.
sentences.zh: 她被匆匆下葬了。

sentences.en: And from that point onwards, among the other Spaniards, there are rumours that he killed her, that he murdered her.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，在其他西班牙人中间，就有传言说他杀了她，他谋杀了她。

sentences.en: He strangled her because she was in the way.
sentences.zh: 他勒死了她，因为她挡了他的路。

sentences.en: Cramping his style.
sentences.zh: 妨碍了他。

sentences.en: Because he lost patience with her, shouting at him about his mistresses.
sentences.zh: 因为他失去了耐心，她一直在对他大喊大叫，抱怨他的情妇们。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: And those rumours never, ever go away.
sentences.zh: 而这些传言从未消失过。

sentences.en: And I don't think you have to be unduly harsh or censorious to think that that is part of a pattern with Cortez.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不必过于苛刻或吹毛求疵，也会认为这符合科尔特斯的一贯作风。

sentences.en: He uses women.
sentences.zh: 他利用女人。

sentences.en: And he dumps them.
sentences.zh: 然后抛弃她们。

sentences.en: And he dumps them.
sentences.zh: 然后又抛弃她们。

sentences.en: And he is a brutal man.
sentences.zh: 他是个残暴的人。

sentences.en: But also, the other thing must be that he has been in command for so long.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，他掌权太久了，这也是原因之一。

sentences.en: And he has been reaching out after what he wants for so long.
sentences.zh: 他追求自己想要的东西已经太久了。

sentences.en: That the idea that he's going to pay attention to the strictures of anyone is a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 所以认为他会听从任何人的约束，简直是痴人说梦。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Because concrete in Australia was the high point in his life.
sentences.zh: 因为征服墨西哥是他人生的高光时刻。

sentences.en: And he doesn't really know what to do with himself, I think, afterwards.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在那之后，他其实不知道该拿自己怎么办。

sentences.en: He clearly fancies himself as the master of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 他显然自认为是墨西哥的主人。

sentences.en: His original plan was to build himself an entirely new capital.
sentences.zh: 他最初的计划是为自己建造一座全新的首都。

sentences.en: So not far from Mexico City, there is an entirely new Spanish city called Puebla.
sentences.zh: 所以离墨西哥城不远，有一座全新的西班牙城市叫普埃布拉。

sentences.en: Beautiful city, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实是一座美丽的城市。

sentences.en: It looks like a Spanish city.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像一座西班牙城市。

sentences.en: And that was their original plan.
sentences.zh: 那本来是他们的最初计划。

sentences.en: But eventually, Cortez clearly fancies the idea of becoming basically the new emperor of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 但最终，科尔特斯显然想成为阿兹特克人的新皇帝。

sentences.en: So rebuilding Tenochtitlan and building a new city on the ruins of the old.
sentences.zh: 所以他重建了特诺奇蒂特兰，并在废墟上建立了一座新城市。

sentences.en: And he will lay claim in inhabiting that city.
sentences.zh: 他将声称自己居住在那座城市里。

sentences.en: He will lay claim to the prestige of Montezuma and his predecessors.
sentences.zh: 他将声称继承蒙特祖马及其前任们的威望。

sentences.en: And so what's impressive about this?
sentences.zh: 那么这有什么令人印象深刻的呢？

sentences.en: And as you say, I mean, they're very beautiful, these buildings that are built in the kind of the earliest years of the Spanish conquest,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我是说，这些在西班牙征服初期建造的建筑非常漂亮，

sentences.en: is that they must be built by Mexican workmen.
sentences.zh: 它们一定是由墨西哥工匠建造的。

sentences.en: Oh, they are.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实如此。

sentences.en: They absolutely are.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, so they adapt to the expectations of Renaissance architecture very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们很快就适应了文艺复兴建筑的期望。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: That's a very good point, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你说得很有道理，汤姆。

sentences.en: So Cortez gets an architect from Europe to design the new city.
sentences.zh: 所以科尔特斯从欧洲找来了一位建筑师来设计这座新城市。

sentences.en: A guy called Alonso García Bravo.
sentences.zh: 一个叫阿隆索·加西亚·布拉沃的人。

sentences.en: The plan is that basically it will be stratified on ethnic lines.
sentences.zh: 计划基本上是按种族界限进行分层。

sentences.en: So the center will be Spanish mansions for the conquistadors.
sentences.zh: 中心地带将是供征服者居住的西班牙式豪宅。

sentences.en: And the Mexica will be confined to the outskirts.
sentences.zh: 而墨西加人将被限制在郊区。

sentences.en: Again, another colonial theme being established.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这又确立了另一种殖民主题。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They tear down the temples.
sentences.zh: 他们拆毁了神庙。

sentences.en: They use the, I mean, could you get greater symbolism?
sentences.zh: 他们利用……我的意思是，还能有比这更具象征意义的吗？

sentences.en: They use the stones of the great temple to build the new cathedral in Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 他们用大神庙的石头在墨西哥城建造了新的大教堂。

sentences.en: A cathedral, which incidentally is currently sinking.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，这座大教堂目前正在下沉。

sentences.en: So the cathedral in Mexico City is gradually collapsing, which is an extraordinary thing.
sentences.zh: 所以墨西哥城的大教堂正在逐渐坍塌，这是一件非同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: They also use the stones to build a massive new palace for Cortez, which still stands.
sentences.zh: 他们还用这些石头为科尔特斯建造了一座巨大的新宫殿，至今仍屹立不倒。

sentences.en: It's in the center of the Zócalo in Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 它位于墨西哥城索卡洛广场的中心。

sentences.en: But as you say,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，

sentences.en: Tom, the people who actually do the work are the Mexica, the Aztecs themselves.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，真正干活的人是墨西加人，也就是阿兹特克人自己。

sentences.en: A visiting friar or monk said that he couldn't believe how enthusiastic they were.
sentences.zh: 一位来访的修士或僧侣说，他简直不敢相信他们竟然如此热心。

sentences.en: He said they seemed to be delighted by doing the work and they were particularly fascinated by the Spanish building technology.
sentences.zh: 他说他们似乎很乐意做这些工作，而且对西班牙的建筑技术特别着迷。

sentences.en: So the carts and the wheelbarrows and the hammers and the chisels made of iron and all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 比如手推车、独轮车、铁锤、铁凿，以及所有这类东西。

sentences.en: Well, this is one of the themes of Camilla Townsend's book, that actually the conquered
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也是卡米拉·汤森德书中的主题之一，即实际上被征服者

sentences.en: don't just sit around and kind of gaze into the abyss, that they do pull themselves together.
sentences.zh: 并不会只是坐着凝视深渊，他们确实振作了起来。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They do say, well, you know, day will follow and night will follow.
sentences.zh: 他们确实会说，嗯，你知道，日复一日，夜复一夜。

sentences.en: And so it goes on and they carry on living.
sentences.zh: 生活就这样继续下去，他们继续过日子。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此。

sentences.en: Because this monk says, there was such a great fervor that the laborers sang and their songs and their voices barely ceased at night.
sentences.zh: 因为这位僧侣说，当时的热情如此高涨，以至于工人们都在唱歌，他们的歌声和声音在夜晚几乎从未停歇。

sentences.en: He's not going to make that up.
sentences.zh: 他没必要编造这种事。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have thought.
sentences.zh: 我倒不这么认为。

sentences.en: So life does go on in a sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，生活确实在继续。

sentences.en: The city ends up being renamed, of course, Ciudad de México, because the Spanish apparently struggle with the name Tenochtitlan,
sentences.zh: 当然，这座城市最终被重新命名为墨西哥城，因为西班牙人显然觉得“特诺奇蒂特兰”这个名字很难念，

sentences.en: but also, of course, a new name signals a new era, though they use the word Mexica,
sentences.zh: 但当然，新名字也标志着一个新时代的到来，尽管他们使用了“墨西加”这个词，

sentences.en: Mexico.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥。

sentences.en: But some of the cities follows the street plan of Tenochtitlan, actually.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，有些城市确实沿用了特诺奇蒂特兰的街道规划。

sentences.en: So you can sort of stand in places and think, you know, I'm standing now where the gate was.
sentences.zh: 所以你有时站在某些地方会想，我知道，我现在站的地方就是以前的城门所在。

sentences.en: And there's a mural where Cortez and Montezuma are supposed to have met.
sentences.zh: 还有一幅壁画，描绘了科尔特斯和蒙特祖玛据称会面的场景。

sentences.en: And there are stretches, aren't there, of canals?
sentences.zh: 而且还有一些运河的遗迹，不是吗？

sentences.en: There are still some canals in the south of the city.
sentences.zh: 在城市南部仍然有一些运河。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: As for the rest of Mexico, the estates that belong to the Mexicas, the emperors and so on, they are parceled out.
sentences.zh: 至于墨西哥的其他地区，属于墨西加人、皇帝等的庄园，都被瓜分了。

sentences.en: They're called encomiendas.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为“监护征赋制”。

sentences.en: Big estates and each encomienda is given to a different conquistador.
sentences.zh: 大庄园，每个监护征赋区都分给了一位不同的征服者。

sentences.en: The landscape itself is changing all the time, of course, because they are bringing over, as in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 当然，景观本身一直在变化，因为他们像在加勒比地区一样，引进了外来物种。

sentences.en: Cows, pigs, sheep, all of these things, and new crops, things like olives and grapevines and things to grow in the new world.
sentences.zh: 牛、猪、羊，所有这些东西，还有新的作物，比如橄榄、葡萄藤，以及在新大陆种植的东西。

sentences.en: But the funny thing about this, you see, what makes it so ambiguous and so interesting is that the people who are working on these lands are not slaves.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，你看，让这一切变得如此模糊且有趣的原因是，在这些土地上工作的人并不是奴隶。

sentences.en: They're more like peasants in feudal, kind of medieval Europe.
sentences.zh: 他们更像是封建中世纪欧洲的农民。

sentences.en: And actually, the question which Camilla Townsend's book, Fifth Son, really brings out is, how much do people notice that something has changed?
sentences.zh: 实际上，卡米拉·汤森德的书《第五个儿子》真正提出的问题是，人们到底有多大程度上注意到发生了变化？

sentences.en: Because up in the villages and away from the centers of habitation, life goes on.
sentences.zh: 因为在村庄里，远离居住中心的地方，生活照旧。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Exactly so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, of course, they're also utterly ravaged by the smallpox.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也受到了天花的彻底蹂躏。

sentences.en: So for most people, I think this is probably the year of the smallpox rather than the Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 所以对大多数人来说，我想这大概是天花之年，而不是西班牙人之年。

sentences.en: If you're working in the fields, do you even see the Spaniards?
sentences.zh: 如果你在田里干活，你甚至能见到西班牙人吗？

sentences.en: You're conscious that your tribute payments go to somebody different.
sentences.zh: 你只是意识到你的贡品交给了不同的人。

sentences.en: And the Aztec aristocracy, it's not like the Norman ConqueSt. They're not all decapitated.
sentences.zh: 而且阿兹特克贵族，这不像诺曼征服。他们并没有被全部斩首。

sentences.en: The heirs of Moctezuma, I mean, this is why they buy into the idea that Moctezuma had submitted to the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 蒙特祖玛的继承人，我的意思是，这就是为什么他们接受了蒙特祖玛已经向西班牙人投降的说法。

sentences.en: It's because it gives them a claim, you know, that they can then use in
sentences.zh: 因为这给了他们一个理由，你知道，他们随后可以在

sentences.en: Spanish law courts to keep hold of their lands.
sentences.zh: 西班牙法庭上利用这一点来保住他们的土地。

sentences.en: They do it very successfully.
sentences.zh: 他们做得非常成功。

sentences.en: Because they end up being treated with respect.
sentences.zh: 因为他们最终受到了尊重。

sentences.en: The Spanish are very, very deferential towards rank and legalism and hierarchy and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人对等级、法制和阶级制度等非常非常讲究。

sentences.en: You have to convert to Christianity to get that.
sentences.zh: 你必须皈依基督教才能获得这些。

sentences.en: If you convert to Christianity, if you say, God, I love Charles V.
sentences.zh: 如果你皈依了基督教，如果你说，上帝啊，我爱查理五世。

sentences.en: I can't get enough of Charles V.
sentences.zh: 我对查理五世爱不释手。

sentences.en: I'm so delighted to be living in this new Spanish imperium.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能生活在这个新的西班牙帝国中。

sentences.en: If you do all these things, then you can have your own estate.
sentences.zh: 如果你做了所有这些事情，那么你就可以拥有自己的庄园。

sentences.en: You can prosper.
sentences.zh: 你可以繁荣昌盛。

sentences.en: You can go to Madrid and sue the king for your historic privileges and all those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你可以去马德里向国王要求你的历史特权以及所有这类事情。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, that's not to say it's sweetness and light and there's not all kinds of exploitation and violence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，这并不是说一切都甜美光明，没有各种剥削和暴力。

sentences.en: Well, Matthew Restless, the final chapter in his book on Moctezuma meeting with Cortez gives a terrifying portrait of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，马修·雷斯特尔在他关于蒙特祖玛会见科尔特斯的书的最后一章中，给出了一个可怕的写照。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know, it's like the kind of Nazi occupation of Poland.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这就像纳粹占领波兰一样。

sentences.en: Mass rape.
sentences.zh: 大规模强奸。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Slaughter.
sentences.zh: 屠杀。

sentences.en: How would you square his portrayal of the horrors of it?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待他对这些恐怖景象的描述？

sentences.en: With Camilla Townsend's.
sentences.zh: 与卡米拉·汤森德的描述相比。

sentences.en: Well, it's not so much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实没那么夸张。

sentences.en: I mean, Camilla Townsend is saying that people, they live lives as they must do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，卡米拉·汤森德说人们过着他们必须过的生活。

sentences.en: But I have also read accounts that say that actually there are whole reaches of
sentences.zh: 但我还读过一些记载，说实际上墨西哥有大片地区

sentences.en: Mexico where the Spanish barely reach, where people continue to worship the old gods.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人几乎没有到达过，那里的人们继续崇拜旧神。

sentences.en: Which is certainly true.
sentences.zh: 这当然是真的。

sentences.en: It would come as news that Tenochtitlan had fallen.
sentences.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰陷落的消息对他们来说简直是新闻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, if you're in the eye of the storm, then it's terrible, but equally, you know, it could just completely pass you by.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果你处于风暴中心，那确实很可怕，但同样，你知道，它也可能完全与你擦肩而过。

sentences.en: I think it's a very complicated picture, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常复杂的情况，汤姆。

sentences.en: And actually to impose one verdict on the whole thing is wrong.
sentences.zh: 实际上，对整件事强加一个定论是错误的。

sentences.en: Because of course there are some places, I mean, Tlashkala most obviously, effectively it's a republic under the King of Spain.
sentences.zh: 因为当然有些地方，比如特拉斯卡拉最明显，它实际上是西班牙国王治下的一个共和国。

sentences.en: Tlashkala's left alone.
sentences.zh: 特拉斯卡拉被留了下来。

sentences.en: Europeans are not allowed to settle in Tlashkala.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人不允许在特拉斯卡拉定居。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They've done brilliantly out of this.
sentences.zh: 他们从中获益匪浅。

sentences.en: They've defeated their age-old enemies.
sentences.zh: 他们击败了宿敌。

sentences.en: They now have a new imperial overlord in the King of Spain, but the King of Spain regards them with, you know, affection because they're his allies.
sentences.zh: 他们现在有了一位新的帝国霸主——西班牙国王，但西班牙国王对他们怀有，你知道，好感，因为他们是他的盟友。

sentences.en: So as far as they're concerned, great, anything but the Mexica.
sentences.zh: 所以对他们来说，太棒了，只要不是墨西加人就行。

sentences.en: If you're one of the Mexica or their allies, life is terrible and you are subject to the violence of the conquistadors.
sentences.zh: 如果你是墨西加人或他们的盟友，生活就很糟糕，你会受到征服者暴力的侵害。

sentences.en: Your family could have been sold into slavery, all of these things.
sentences.zh: 你的家人可能被卖为奴隶，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: But if you're in an outlying region, and particularly the further away from
sentences.zh: 但如果你在偏远地区，特别是离

sentences.en: Tenochtitlan you are, and the more rural, the more difficult to reach, the chances are you could live your life and never lay eyes on a Spaniard, I would guess.
sentences.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰越远，越偏僻，越难到达的地方，我猜你很可能一辈子都见不到一个西班牙人。

sentences.en: And of course, in some of these parts that are really difficult to reach, in the Yucatan, for example, I mean, there...
sentences.zh: 当然，在一些真正难以到达的地方，比如尤卡坦半岛，我的意思是，那里……

sentences.en: They still supposedly worship Tlaloc to this day, apparently.
sentences.zh: 据说直到今天，人们似乎还在崇拜特拉洛克。

sentences.en: I don't know if that's true or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是不是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, there are parts that are not even nominally conquered until the end of the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些地区直到17世纪末甚至名义上都没有被征服。

sentences.en: So the idea that the conquest of Mexico is done and dusted by the early 1520s is obviously completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以认为墨西哥的征服在1520年代初就已完成并结束的想法显然是完全错误的。

sentences.en: And Dominic, one other thing that happens within, what, a decade of the fall of Tenochtitlan is that the Virgin Mary appears to a peasant.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，在特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后的十年内，还发生了一件事，那就是圣母玛利亚向一位农民显灵。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I thought we'd get onto that.
sentences.zh: 我以为我们会谈到这个。

sentences.en: And speaks to him in Nahuatl.
sentences.zh: 并用纳瓦特尔语对他说话。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's the Virgin of Guadalupe, who supposedly appears to a guy called Juan Diego, who gets a sort of image imprinted on his cloak.
sentences.zh: 这就是瓜达卢佩圣母，据说她向一个叫胡安·迭戈的人显灵，他的斗篷上印上了一种图像。

sentences.en: What is so interesting about that story,
sentences.zh: 关于那个故事最有趣的是，

sentences.en: Tom, is first of all, it probably didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，首先，它可能根本没发生过。

sentences.en: Because the accounts that we have come are later, and it's probably been kind of back projected.
sentences.zh: 因为我们拥有的记载都是后来的，而且它很可能是被某种程度上追溯投射的。

sentences.en: And secondly, the place where that happens, which is a hill called Tepeac, which is north of Lake Texcoco, was already a pilgrimage site.
sentences.zh: 其次，发生这件事的地方，也就是特佩亚克山，在特斯科科湖北部，本身就是一个朝圣地。

sentences.en: I think this is a really interesting element of the story.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是故事中一个非常有趣的元素。

sentences.en: So it had been sacred to the Aztec goddesses Tonantzin and Chico Mecoatl, who are the goddesses of the earth and a farming kind of fertility.
sentences.zh: 所以它对阿兹特克女神托南辛和奇科梅科亚特尔来说是神圣的，她们是大地和农业丰产的女神。

sentences.en: So very like the way that the Parthenon, the temple to Athena, becomes a church dedicated to the Virgin.
sentences.zh: 这很像雅典娜神庙帕台农神庙变成供奉圣母的教堂的方式。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So when people are going to this shrine, the shrine of the Virgin of Guadalupe, they are not necessarily completely breaking with the traditions of their ancestors.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们去这个圣地，即瓜达卢佩圣母圣地时，他们并不一定完全切断了祖先的传统。

sentences.en: They're actually going to the same place their ancestors might well have gone to.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在去他们祖先很可能去过的地方。

sentences.en: But also the Virgin weeps over the sufferings of her dead son.
sentences.zh: 而且圣母也为她死去的儿子的苦难而哭泣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I wonder if that is a way in for people to this new understanding of the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想知道这是否是人们理解这种新超自然现象的一种途径。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, Tom, on the religious element, I know the religious element you obviously find fascinating and understandably so.
sentences.zh: 不，汤姆，关于宗教因素，我知道你显然觉得宗教因素很迷人，这也可以理解。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the most obvious of all the changes that sweeps over what they call New Spain, what becomes Mexico.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是席卷他们所谓的“新西班牙”（即后来的墨西哥）的所有变化中最明显的一个。

sentences.en: But even then it's so complicated because it's quite syncretic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，它也非常复杂，因为它相当融合，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The friars who arrive in Mexico, they say, well, we've got to make allowances for these people.
sentences.zh: 抵达墨西哥的修士们说，好吧，我们必须体谅这些人。

sentences.en: We've got to allow them to keep up some of their old custoMs. So for example, they're very happy to allow the indigenous Mexican people to worship in open air chapels that are like
sentences.zh: 我们必须允许他们保留一些旧习俗。所以例如，他们非常乐意允许墨西哥原住民在露天礼拜堂中进行礼拜，这些礼拜堂就像

sentences.en: their old temples.
sentences.zh: 他们以前的神庙一样。

sentences.en: And the stonemasons who carve the things in the new chapels, the old gods are often depicted alongside Jesus and Mary.
sentences.zh: 而在新礼拜堂雕刻东西的石匠，旧神经常被描绘在耶稣和玛利亚旁边。

sentences.en: And there are even some claims, I don't know how true this is because it's all perhaps sounds too good to be true, that they use the old sacrificial stones
sentences.zh: 甚至有人声称，我不知道这有多真实，因为这一切听起来可能太好而不像是真的，他们用旧的祭祀石

sentences.en: to build altars and things.
sentences.zh: 来建造祭坛之类的东西。

sentences.en: I just wonder whether the story of-
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道关于……的故事是否……

sentences.en: Suffering and the underdog.
sentences.zh: 苦难和弱者。

sentences.en: The suffering-
sentences.zh: 苦难……

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And resurrection.
sentences.zh: 以及复活。

sentences.en: Because the idea of life coming from the dead is what underpins the cult of
sentences.zh: 因为生命源于死亡的想法是希佩托特克崇拜的基础。

sentences.en: Chippitotec.
sentences.zh: 你知道，披着剥下的皮四处游荡可能看起来离受难日很远，但那里确实有一种从最凄凉的绝望中涌现出希望的叙事，

sentences.en: You know, wandering around in flayed skins might seem a long way from Good Friday, but there is a kind of narrative there of hope emerging from the bleakest despair that perhaps
sentences.zh: 也许这确实能引起人们的共鸣。

sentences.en: does speak to people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，墨西哥最终确实成为了一个非常天主教的国家。

sentences.en: I mean, Mexico does end up a very Catholic country.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我对它了解不够。

sentences.en: I don't know enough about it.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为这非常可信，但还有另一个因素，当然，

sentences.en: Tom, I think that's very plausible, but there's another element to it, which is, of course,
sentences.zh: 基督教是胜利者的宗教。

sentences.en: Christianity is the religion of the winners.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是不言而喻的，但这一直是基督教的一个悖论。

sentences.en: I mean, that absolutely goes without saying, but it has always been a paradox of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它是胜利者的宗教。

sentences.en: You know, it is a religion of the winners.
sentences.zh: 它是全世界信徒最多的宗教。

sentences.en: It's the most practiced religion across the world.
sentences.zh: 它是全世界信徒最多的宗教。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it offers a peculiar sense of identification with the divine to those who have suffered, those who have been tortured or persecuted.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，对于那些遭受过苦难、遭受过酷刑或迫害的人来说，它提供了一种与神同在的独特认同感。

sentences.en: Yeah, but not to dwell on that, rather to dwell on the fact that this is one of the stories that you've chosen to tell.

sentences.en: The risks that Cortez takes, but also for the drama of this kind of unique meeting of two great powers from different worlds, kind of almost different time zones.

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些出于完全可以理解的原因，在意识形态上非常、非常

sentences.en: opposed to everything that, say, Cortez represents, are they justified in being nervous of the sheer drama of this story?

sentences.en: So Matthew Restor, for example, is explicit in his book in saying, you know, I want to take out the glamour from this story and the melodrama.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如马修·雷斯托在书中明确表示，你知道，我想从这个故事中剔除魅力和情节剧。

sentences.en: I want to show it as a horrible, you know, he loathes Cortez.
sentences.zh: 我想把它展示为一个可怕的……你知道，他厌恶科尔特斯。

sentences.en: He hates the Spanish project, if you like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，他讨厌西班牙人的计划。

sentences.en: He thinks it represents rape, torture, slavery, exploitation, all of these things.
sentences.zh: 他认为这代表了强奸、酷刑、奴役、剥削，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: I don't think I'm putting words in his mouth.
sentences.zh: 我想我没有曲解他的意思。

sentences.en: And he would say, to tell it in a kind of roaring, swashbuckling style is to give them what they want, is to miss what he sees as the horrible realism of the story.
sentences.zh: 他会说，用那种轰轰烈烈、剑侠风格的方式来讲述它，就是给他们想要的东西，就是忽略了他所看到的这个故事中可怕的现实主义。

sentences.en: So is that what we've done in the series?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们在本系列中就是这样做的吗？

sentences.en: I think when the rest is history, and actually not just on the rest is history, I think lots of historical work more generally has its cake and eats it, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我认为当谈到《余下的历史》时，实际上不仅仅是《余下的历史》，我认为许多历史著作在更广泛的意义上都想要两全其美，不是吗？

sentences.en: Music and eating chicken Kiev or whatever, and not actually having fun at all.

sentences.en: Hanging out on Carnaby Street.
sentences.zh: 在卡纳比街闲逛。

sentences.en: But I have my cake and eat it in those books.

sentences.en: I have long descriptions of Carnaby Street and the Beatles and all of that stuff, while also saying, actually, most people have very humdrum lives, just like you, when you write

sentences.en: about the Romans and you tell the most fantastic stories about the emperors.

sentences.en: But you see, I think doing it now and just, I'm thinking aloud, really thinking how I feel about the story that we've been telling.
sentences.zh: 但你看，我认为现在这样做……我只是在自言自语，真的在思考我对我们一直在讲述的故事的感受。

sentences.en: I think actually I would come to a slightly different conclusion, which is that humans love these kinds of stories.
sentences.zh: 我想实际上我会得出一个稍微不同的结论，那就是人类喜欢这类故事。

sentences.zh: 他们当然喜欢，汤姆。

sentences.en: Even if the stories end in tragedy and horror, we still love them.
sentences.zh: 即使这些故事以悲剧和恐怖告终，我们依然热爱它们。

sentences.en: So throughout these episodes, you know, there've been echoes of Greek tragedy, biblical accounts of the fall of Jerusalem, classical history.

sentences.en: And these are great stories as well.
sentences.zh: 这些也都是伟大的故事。

sentences.en: And the horror is interfused with the drama and the excitement.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think there is no escaping from the fact that the horror isn't something that can be divorced from the drama.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为不可否认的事实是，恐怖并不是可以从戏剧性中剥离出来的东西。

sentences.en: It's kind of interfused.

sentences.en: I totally agree.

sentences.en: And it says something unsettling, perhaps, about human nature and about human desire for stories.

sentences.en: And what we want from history.
sentences.zh: 以及我们从历史中想要得到什么。

sentences.en: I completely agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的观点。

sentences.en: And that's why actually the difference between writing for children and writing for adults is not as great as one might think.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么实际上为儿童写作和为成人写作之间的区别并不像人们想象的那么大。

sentences.en: So when you're writing for children, you're very conscious that ultimately what most of them will crave is action, excitement.
sentences.zh: 所以当你为孩子们写作时，你会非常清楚，他们最终渴望的大多是动作和刺激。

sentences.en: They love the horror, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们喜欢恐怖。

sentences.en: I mean, I know because I go into schools to talk to groups, sometimes quite small children, children eight or nine or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道，因为我经常去学校和小组交谈，有时是相当小的孩子，八九岁的孩子之类的。

sentences.en: They can't get enough of Henry VIII having an enema or people having their heads chopped off by the guillotine or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 他们对亨利八世灌肠或者人们被断头台砍头之类的故事百听不厌。

sentences.en: Now, we all laugh about that and we say, ah, kids, they're very bloodthirsty.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们都对此付之一笑，说，啊，孩子们，他们真是嗜血。

sentences.en: But actually, adults are no different.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，成年人也没什么不同。

sentences.en: If you look at the podcasts that we've done, they get the most, you know, the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看我们做过的播客，它们获得了最多的……你知道，纳粹那期。

sentences.en: But I think with this, there's another reason why it's such an incredible story, which is that there is heroism on both sides.
sentences.zh: 但我认为关于这一点，它之所以成为一个如此不可思议的故事还有另一个原因，那就是双方都有英雄主义。

sentences.en: Yeah, agreed.
sentences.zh: 没错，同意。

sentences.zh: 所以科尔特斯，无论你怎么看他，我的意思是，他显然是个可怕的人，但他的勇气和赌博的意愿使得人们几乎不可能在阅读所发生的事情时

sentences.en: and not feel a sense of admiration for him.
sentences.zh: 而不对他产生一种钦佩之情。

sentences.zh: 而且我认为也发生了什么，特别是对于那些

sentences.en: And the tragedy when they lose.
sentences.zh: 以及他们失败时的悲剧。

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我想这就是悲剧或伟大故事的精髓，你可以阅读或聆听这个故事，并认同科尔特斯所尝试的胆识，同时为这个非凡文明所遭受的恐怖感到悲伤。

sentences.en: boldness of what Cortez is attempting and feel the kind of grief for the horror that is visited on this extraordinary civilization.
sentences.zh: 你可以同时感受到这两者。

sentences.zh: 这或许是这个故事独特力量的一部分。

sentences.en: And that's part of the power, perhaps, uniquely of this story.
sentences.zh: 我想不出还有什么地方的这种张力如此强烈。

sentences.zh: 我完全同意，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人们习惯将其描述为邪恶的阿兹特克人和勇敢的西班牙人之间的冲突。

sentences.en: For centuries, people used to tell it as a clash between wicked Aztecs and gallant Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 如今，从相反的角度来讲述它更为普遍，将阿兹特克人描绘成高贵的弱者，将西班牙征服者描绘成贪婪的怪物。

sentences.en: These days, it's more common to tell it from the opposite angle, casting the Aztecs as noble underdogs and the Spanish conquerors as greedy monsters.
sentences.zh: 但我并不这么看。

sentences.en: But I don't see it that way.
sentences.zh: 双方都有很多残忍，但也有很多勇气。

sentences.en: There was plenty of cruelty on both sides, but plenty of courage too.
sentences.zh: 蒙特祖马是英雄吗？

sentences.zh: 或者那样想是否有点过于简单化了？

sentences.en: Or is it a bit simplistic to think of them that way?
sentences.zh: 真知灼见。

sentences.zh: 我认为这正是我们作为撰写此事的历史学家应该采取的方法。

sentences.en: And I think that's exactly the approach that actually we should take as historians writing about this.
sentences.zh: 将这些人视为一个世界中的行动者，在那里他们感到非常困惑，试图弄清楚正在发生什么。

sentences.en: To see these people as actors in a world where they're very confused, they're trying to make sense of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 这是一个前所未有的情况。
